SPECIAL INTEREST GROUPS
Before describing a specific assortment of telecom special interest groups, we need to understand some of the legal and ethical requirements of special interest groups.
DISCUSSION

Special interest groups are usually involved for reasons that do not include immediate monetary gain. That is to say, the group is not making profits from operations or sales. These organizations are called non-profit organizations...
Non-profit organizations must not distribute income to members or attract private investors. They may act as a corporation in all other respects with few exceptions.

In the USA, non-profit organization regulations are published in the C.F.R. (Code of Federal Regulations) and state requirements. Specifically, Title 26 of the US Code, Internal Revenue Service procedures, which defines the non-profit organization...

US states further define the non-profit organization and establish legal requirements such as licenses, charters, and privileges. Some states make distinctions based on chartered charitable goals. If the organization supports charities, privileges will be granted accordingly...

Not all telecommunications industry special interest groups are non-profit organizations. Some are actually clubs that do not receive any privileges. Others are international and follow the codes of commerce between nations. Yet others only exist in cyber space....

Telecom special interest groups have a hierarchy. The FORUM is the highest status. Organizations that wear the title Forum are well established and influential. Committees, associations, and industry groups have valuable contributions to make, but seem to occupy lower status...

The word forum means a meeting place where orations are delivered. A forum today is the same as the original in concept, but the actual place may be undefined or, as described in Internet terms, in cyber space. The only requirements for forums are a subject of interest and that they have more than 1 member..

The ATM Forum creates specification standards for industry using working groups of members. The working groups vote on initiatives and/or reach a consensus on matters. Technical working groups include, but are not limited to:
1. Control Signaling - dynamic operation and protocol
2. Network Management - ATM network issues
3. Security - technology security matters
4. Testing - performance and acceptance testing standards
5. Voice and Multimedia - communications adaptability

Special interest groups provide information and a place to go for open discussion on a particular aspect of the technology. It is a good idea to join clubs, associations, and discussion groups in the career field of choice. Newsletters and hot air are not the only benefits a special interest group has to offer...
Career networking, leadership opportunities, and technical training are also benefits of a special interest group.

Career networking is the best way to advance in a high tech line of work. Telecom professionals may work for several companies, or become self-employed, during the span of a career. Forming a network of colleagues and business acquaintances is automatically part of the special interest group membership.....

Another benefit is leadership and technical training. Participation in a special interest group includes political and social interaction. Members can be elected to officer positions in the group, like chairman. The technical skills are obvious, but the leadership and team skills experience may be difficult to get anywhere else in the workplace.....

The new forum will receive start up assistance from Nida Corporation and TIMA. The forum will be a non-profit organization that supports at least one scholarship fund (charity). The FCC will be the regulatory body...

The next decision to be made is a big one: incorporate or not? Becoming incorporated has significant advantages, especially in non-profit organizations. The forum is a business. The product is standardization and configuration control and the monies raised from sales are applied to a scholarship fund. Operating costs are covered by membership dues and renewal fees.....

Incorporating has many benefits. If the founder leaves, the forum stays. The organization is a registered entity. The name is copyrighted and individual ownership is not a controlling factor. Having the title Inc. added to the name lends credibility and makes it easier to find supporters and sponsors...

Incorporating takes extra work, but it's worth it in this case. Now that the forum will be incorporated officially, most of the organizational planning can be done by a consulting company or small business support group. The forum's sponsors will usually fund the incorporation effort...

The forum will have a board of directors, administrative assistant, Webmaster, and member companies. Bylaws will need to be established to govern the operating procedures of the forum. Legal assistance is required to ensure the bylaws are consistent with federal and state law...

The board of directors will be headed by an elected chairman. The board is charged with forum strategic planning, public information releases, convention planning, and quality management. The board ensures the forum operates as an ethical non-profit business. The membership executes the mission of the forum.....
